title: Ankhorage Atlas
summary: Analyzes codebases, dependencies, architecture rules, and audit evidence through an interactive graph workspace and CLI.
purpose: Provide inspectable evidence about source projects and their architecture while keeping reusable graph, dependency, and project-detection behavior in their dedicated packages.
responsibilities: Analyze local paths and GitHub repositories into project, dependency, and audit evidence.
Render interactive graph and audit workspaces.
Expose audit, inspect, and export capabilities through its CLI provider.
Export portable Atlas reports and offline workspaces.
boundaries: Does not replace the dedicated project detection, graph, graph-to-Cytoscape, or dependency-analysis packages.
Does not own repository authentication or source materialization providers.
Does not make architecture policy reusable by duplicating rules owned by rule-provider packages.
audience: Developers and architecture reviewers investigating source-project structure and dependencies.
Tooling integrations that need Atlas audit, inspection, or export capabilities.
useCases: Inspect a local project or GitHub repository as an interactive dependency graph.
Run an architecture audit and retain evidence for its findings.
Export a portable Atlas report or offline workspace.

architecture.role: Application and CLI composition layer over canonical project, dependency, graph, audit, and visualization boundaries.
invariants: Reusable analysis and graph behavior is consumed through released public APIs of its owning packages.
Audits provide evidence suitable for UI and build-tool integrations.
The interactive workspace remains a consumer of reusable analysis contracts rather than their duplicate owner.

limitations: Repository access and source acquisition depend on explicit configured capabilities or adapters.
Atlas does not claim to support every language or build-system analyzer.
